heading: EXT. SHRINKING SANDBAR - TIDAL FLAT - DAWN

units.text: EXT. SHRINKING SANDBAR - TIDAL FLAT - DAWN
A strip of gray sand a hundred yards long, ringed by a pale, rising sea.
Gulls wheel overhead.
In the distance, the mainland is a blue smear.
TALITHA OKORAFOR-BENNET, twenties, sits on an upturned crate with a battered voice recorder in her lap.
Her boots are soaked.
A blue tarp is staked beside her, whipping in the wind.
She has not slept.
She presses RECORD.
A red light blinks.
Day two. Survey boat Dunlin is gone. I'm on the sandbar south of Gannet Point. Tide's rising. I have maybe forty minutes.
units.name: TALITHA

units.text: She stops.
Rewinds a few seconds.
Plays it back.
...Tide's rising. I have maybe forty minutes.
units.name: TALITHA

units.text: She nods.
The water, closer than a minute ago, licks at the crate.
She stands, planting her boots in the sand, and ties the recorder inside her vest.
Not going anywhere.
units.name: TALITHA

units.text: She unclips her flare gun and loads it, slow and deliberate.
Lifts it overhead.
The flare shoots up and bursts red against the dawn.
She watches it fall.
She sits again on the crate as the tide reaches her ankles.
She takes the recorder out and presses RECORD.
If anyone finds this, I stayed with the boat's last known position. I did everything right.
units.name: TALITHA

units.text: The water climbs her shins.
She keeps her eyes on the blue smear of the mainland and does not look down.
